decisions.question: The Boundary rows for `Bus`, `Publisher` and `Bus.publisher` (bus-api@v1), `TestBus` (bus-testing@v1), `TopologyBuilder.write` and `TopologyBuilder.reduceInto` (topology-dsl@v1) and `PageScope` and `FlutterNavigationExecutor` (flutter-binding@v1), the Terms bullets Application code (bus-testing@v1, flutter-binding@v1 G17) and Recognition (bus-api@v1 For static analysis), and the `global_bus_accessor` rule detail (bus-api@v1 For static analysis) cite versions H2, H3, H4 and H6 superseded. Move them, and does any of them change meaning?

options.label: move to v2, no rewording
options.consequence: the rows and bullets name the versions consumers build against; holds only if the cited text still says what these sentences rely on

options.label: keep v1
options.consequence: violates DEC-688 and the intake record's rule that every live citation moves inside the intake; gate.mjs --final would warn

decisions.why: Each sentence only assigns ownership or cites a definition, and the cited text carries over. bus-api@v2's For static analysis section is identical to v1's (diff against a313ab0, the last v1 commit), so Recognition and the accessor definition, getters included, still hold. bus-api@v2, bus-testing@v2 and topology-dsl@v2 changed no declaration; flutter-binding@v2 added `NidanaModule` and kept `PageScope` and `FlutterNavigationExecutor` unchanged in shape. `TestBus` still extends `Bus` in `nidana_dart_runtime`, so 'Bus matches the class and every subclass, TestBus included' holds. flutter-binding@v2 G17 is wider (start()'s connections recorded, `input` and `stub` usable before start()), but the Application code bullet relies only on test code claiming topics through `stub`, which G17 still states.

decisions.question: Check (2) of the step: do bus-api@v2's `Bus.publisher` and its G20, and flutter-binding@v2 G7 and G14, which the claim-site table and the claim resolution bullet cite, still name the same arguments (`route`, `name`, `writes`, `scope`, the source), so the claim recognition stays true when the citations move?

options.label: move, recognition unchanged
options.consequence: the four claim sites, their argument names and the stand-in source rule stay as v1 states them; the scan cases need no change

options.label: restate the claim-site table
options.consequence: needed only if an argument was renamed or a default changed; any change to what is claimed is breaking under this contract's Versioning (a new claim site, or a write set that newly resolves)

decisions.why: `Bus.publisher(MessageSource source, {Set<StateTopic<Object?>> writes, Scope scope = Scope.application})` is identical in bus-api@v2 (only its line moved); bus-api@v2 G20 is word for word v1's; `PageScope({String? route, List<Topology> topologies, Set<StateTopic<Object?>> writes, required Widget child})` and flutter-binding@v2 G7 differ from v1 only in citing bus-api@v2 G20; `FlutterNavigationExecutor(Bus bus, {..., String name = 'flutter-navigation', ...})` and G14 are unchanged. So the table's Source, Scope and Write set columns and the `flutter-navigation` default still read off the cited declarations.

decisions.question: Check (1) of the step: does flutter-binding@v2's new `NidanaModule(moduleId, topologies, gracePeriod, child)` need recognizing here, as a claim site or in the Boundary?

options.label: no, not a claim site
options.consequence: the four-site table and G11's 'no other construct claims' stay; the module's topologies reach the scan through the graph document like any other topology

options.label: recognize it
options.consequence: a new claim site is breaking under this contract's Versioning ('reporting more than v1 reports ... a new claim site') and would need nidana-checks@v2; and there is nothing to claim, since it takes no `writes`

decisions.why: flutter-binding@v2 G20: `NidanaModule` declares a module with `bus.module(...)` and acquires a reference at mount; it constructs no publisher and takes no `writes`, so it makes no shell claim. The writes of the topologies it activates are topology writes, which the scan reads from the graph document that `catalog` writes from the explicit `catalogTopologies()` list (Refinement 2; S72 confirmed the catalog needs nothing for `NidanaModule`). `ModuleScopeObserver` and `ModuleRoutes`, which v1 already had, were never claim sites for the same reason. The Boundary rows name only declarations this contract recognizes, so `NidanaModule` is not added there either; G11 already excludes it.
evidence: hsdd/contract/nidana-checks.md Refinement 2, G11, Versioning Breaking list

decisions.question: Topic declarations says a name that is not a string literal is reported `unresolved_topic_name` and 'the bus's own check covers it (bus-api@v1 G7)'. bus-api@v2 restated G7. Move the citation as is, or restate the sentence?

options.label: move, sentence stays
options.consequence: the sentence keeps relying only on the runtime's name check existing for every declaration

options.label: restate per v2 G7
options.consequence: would copy v2's wording (first use compared, tracing, removal frees the name) into this contract, which owns none of it

decisions.why: v2 G7 compares every access and every claim with the declaration registered under its name, 'the first use of each declaration included', where v1 G7 compared accesses after the first. That is a stronger statement of the same check, so 'the bus's own check covers' a name the scan cannot read is at least as true under v2. The cited guarantee was restated, not renumbered; reported in notes_for_orchestrator, not reworded.

decisions.question: Refinement 4 says 'bus-api@v1 G40 leaves one gap ... so `bus.publish<num, double>(intEvents, 1.5)` compiles and fails at run time' and 'topology-dsl@v1's `write` and `reduceInto` have the same gap'. bus-api@v2 G41 changed what happens to an off-type value after publish. Move as is, or restate the run-time half?

options.label: move, sentence stays
options.consequence: Refinement 4 keeps its reason for the rule in one clause; the detail of the run-time failure stays bus-api's

options.label: restate the run-time failure per v2 G41
options.consequence: would spell out that the publish passes unchecked and each subscription or read that cannot convert gets a TypeError (a read ending its write chains); more text owned by bus-api, no change to the rule

decisions.why: bus-api@v2 G40 is word for word v1's, including 'explicit type arguments can still widen the topic's type ... outside this guarantee'. Under v2 G41 the off-type value is checked neither by the publish nor by the delivery, and each subscription or topology read that cannot convert it receives a `TypeError` (a read's ends every write chain it reaches, G26), so the call still compiles and fails at run time. topology-dsl@v2 keeps `write<T, S extends T>(Topic<T>, TopicStream<S>)` and `reduceInto<S, E>` unchanged, so the same gap exists there. The sentence stays true; the Versioning touch entry records why.

decisions.question: Versioning amendment (a), drained 2026-10-18, says the rule detail 'cites bus-api@v1 For static analysis, which since that contract's amendment (f) defines a global bus accessor exactly as G5 reports it'. Live or historical?

options.label: keep v1 (historical)
options.consequence: the dated amendment keeps describing the version its amendment (f) changed

options.label: move to v2
options.consequence: would misdate the amendment: bus-api's amendment (f) is a v1 amendment

decisions.why: It is a dated amendment entry describing what bus-api@v1's amendment (f) did; the intake record's rule keeps the version historical text describes.

decisions.question: S66 observed that two modules declaring one topology id with IR-equal but `==`-unequal plans count once in a TopologyGraph, though bus-api@v2 G23 rejects the second activation, and said the gap, if it matters, belongs to topic-codegen or nidana-checks. Does Not here's sentence on duplicate topology ids, or any check, need to change?

options.label: leave Not here as is
options.consequence: the scan keeps reading only what a graph document holds; a G23 conflict stays a run-time check

options.label: add a scan finding for it
options.consequence: impossible from a JSON graph, which holds no functions; and a new scan check is breaking under this contract's Versioning

decisions.why: The scan reads JSON graph documents (Refinement 2) that carry no closures, so it cannot compare plan functions with `==`. topology-ir@v1 G11 counts IR-equal definitions once, so 'a graph the scan reads never holds two' stays true. S72 reached the same answer for the catalog. Recorded in the Versioning touch entry.
